alt: A table of names and scores fills in one row at a time. Each row prints with the name left-aligned in 10 characters and the score right-aligned in 5, so every score's last digit lines up under the one above it.

steps.caption: Row 0: f"{name:<10}{score:>5}" left-aligns "Ana" in 10 characters and right-aligns 92 in 5.
Row 1: f"{name:<10}{score:>5}" left-aligns "Bo" in 10 characters and right-aligns 7 in 5.
Row 2: f"{name:<10}{score:>5}" left-aligns "Charlie" in 10 characters and right-aligns 100 in 5.
Every row lines up under the last one: the name column always starts at position 0, and the score column always ends at position 14, however long each name or score is.
Row 0: f"{name:<10}{score:>5}" left-aligns "Al" in 10 characters and right-aligns 3 in 5.
Row 1: f"{name:<10}{score:>5}" prints "Christopher" in its own 11 characters, past the 10-character minimum and right-aligns 150 in 5.

"Christopher" is 11 characters, more than the 10-character field. A width in a format spec is only a minimum: it never cuts text short, so this row's score field starts later than a shorter name's would.
